Maia for Interview debrief preparation

Organize interview evidence for the hiring team's review.

Give interviewers a shared evidence summary without turning notes into an automatic ranking. Maia prepares the debrief while the hiring team owns evaluation and selection.

All use cases ↗

Use authorized interview material

Provide the approved evaluation criteria, interview plan, and notes that the hiring panel may access. Keep candidate information in the designated private channel. Remove details unrelated to job evaluation.

Ask Maia to preserve which interviewer supplied each observation and when. It should not merge several comments into a stronger claim than any interviewer made.

Organize evidence by criterion

The packet can group direct observations under each approved criterion and link back to the note. It should distinguish observed behavior, interviewer interpretation, and a score when the process uses one.

If the notes do not cover a criterion, mark the evidence missing. Do not infer ability from a resume line or another criterion. Unapproved factors should remain outside the evaluation.

Preserve conflicting views

Debriefs are useful because interviewers may interpret evidence differently. Maia should show disagreement and the supporting notes rather than averaging it away. The hiring lead can ask each interviewer to explain their judgment.

The same applies to vague praise or concern. "Strong communicator" needs the observed example and its relevance to the role.

Prepare the discussion, not the verdict

The hiring team reviews the packet, corrects errors, supplies missing scorecards, and discusses the evidence. Maia can capture questions and summarize the final decision only after the authorized owner records it.

It should not rank candidates, infer protected characteristics, or make the hiring choice. Human reviewers remain responsible for consistent, job-related evaluation.

Start with a completed process

Use a past interview set that your hiring lead may review. Compare Maia's organization with the original debrief and check whether it preserves nuance and source attribution. Fix the criteria or note format when interviewers repeatedly leave important evidence unclear.

Questions from hiring teams

Can Maia score a candidate?

It can organize scores that interviewers already supplied under approved criteria. The hiring team owns evaluation and the final decision.

What if feedback is late?

Mark the scorecard missing and proceed according to your hiring process. Maia should not fill the gap from other interviews.

Where should the packet live?

Use a restricted Slack channel or approved hiring system whose audience may access the candidate information.

Delete or retain working material according to the organization's hiring-record rules. The debrief packet should not become a separate, indefinite store for candidate information merely because the discussion happened in Slack.

The hiring lead remains responsible for that record decision.
